subject.title: fix(memory): hide QMD transport metadata from recalled content

question: Should existing QMD-contaminated short-term recall rows be repaired from their source ranges, discarded as rebuildable cache, or intentionally allowed to age out after this adapter fix?
rationale: Stored rows do not clearly preserve backend provenance, so automation cannot safely choose between preserving recall history and avoiding false-positive modification of legitimate diff content.

options.title: Repair or discard contaminated rows
options.body: Add a plugin-owned upgrade path that rehydrates confidently attributable rows from source and drops only rows that cannot be repaired safely.

options.title: Accept bounded age-out
options.body: Merge the adapter-only fix and explicitly document that existing contaminated recall rows may continue affecting Dreaming until normal retention removes them.

recommendation.title: Repair or discard contaminated rows
recommendation.body: Add a plugin-owned upgrade path that rehydrates confidently attributable rows from source and drops only rows that cannot be repaired safely.

likelyOwner.reason: This contributor's merged history covers both the QMD adapter and the original Dreaming recall-store behavior involved in the decision.
